claims.text: JPMorgan Chase & Co.'s common equity tier 1 capital ratio was 15.0% actual in 2023:Q4, projected 13.4% at 2026:Q1 ending, and projected minimum 12.5% under the severely adverse scenario, per Table A.17 of the 2024 Federal Reserve Stress Test Results.

citations.quotation: Table A.17. JPMorgan Chase & Co. Projected stressed capital ratios, loan losses, risk-weighted assets, losses, revenues, and net income before taxes Federal Reserve estimates: Severely adverse scenario ... Item Actual 2023:Q4 Projected 2026:Q1 Projected minimum Common equity tier 1 capital ratio 15.0 13.4 12.5

Capital ratios and risk-weighted assets, actual 2023:Q4 and projected 2024:Q1–2026:Q1 ... These projections represent hypothetical estimates that involve an economic outcome that is more adverse than expected.

claims.text: The 12.5% figure in Table 6's summary list also appears as JPMorgan Chase's minimum CET1 ratio for the 2024:Q1–2026:Q1 period, consistent with Table A.17's projected minimum.

citations.quotation: JPMorgan Chase 12.5 ... The minimum capital ratio presented is for the period 2024:Q1 to 2026:Q1. Source: Federal Reserve estimates in the severely adverse scenario.

counterarguments.text: The 12.5% value in the Table 6 excerpt appears without its column header directly attached in the excerpt; it could theoretically be an ending rather than minimum ratio, but the note stating 'The minimum capital ratio presented is for the period 2024:Q1 to 2026:Q1' supports it being the projected minimum.

citations.quotation: JPMorgan Chase 12.5 ... Note: The capital ratios are calculated using the capital action assumptions provided within the supervisory stress testing rules.

limitations: Source excerpts are partial; the full Table 6 column headers for JPMorgan Chase's row are not visible in the excerpt, so the bank-specific Table A.17 is used as the primary evidence.
The source text notes that data for JPMorgan Chase in table A.32 (page 57) was revised on August 28, 2024; the excerpts do not show whether Table A.17 values were affected.

Projections are hypothetical estimates under a severely adverse scenario, not forecasts of actual outcomes; capital ratios use supervisory capital action assumptions per 12 C.F.R. §§ 238.132(d); 252.44(c).
